lead-qualifier.name: Lead Qualifier
lead-qualifier.description: Normalise an inbound lead, check company size, and label it hot or nurture.
lead-qualifier.sample: One inbound lead with a name, an email and the company size.
lead-qualifier.result: The lead labelled hot (50 or more employees) or nurture.

ticket-priority.name: Ticket Priority Router
ticket-priority.description: Score a support ticket by keywords and route urgent ones to an escalation output.
ticket-priority.sample: One support ticket with a subject and the customer's plan.
ticket-priority.result: The ticket saved as escalate or standard queue. Nobody is notified.

order-totals.name: Order Totals Digest
order-totals.description: Add up an order's line items and flag orders over $250 for review. No discount is applied.
order-totals.sample: One order with two lines, each with a quantity and a price.
order-totals.result: The order total and line count, saved as needing review or not.

low-stock-list.name: Low Stock List
low-stock-list.description: Find the products at or below their reorder level and list them by how many are missing. It only makes a list — nothing is ordered.
low-stock-list.sample: Six products, each with the amount on hand and a reorder level.
low-stock-list.result: The products to restock, largest shortfall first, or how many products were checked when nothing is low.

invoice-follow-up-list.name: Invoice Follow-up List
invoice-follow-up-list.description: List unpaid invoices that are past due on the date you choose, with days overdue and the total. It only makes a list — no reminders are sent.
invoice-follow-up-list.sample: Five invoices in one currency, whether each is paid, and the date to check on.
invoice-follow-up-list.result: The overdue invoices, oldest first, with days overdue and the total due.

quote-calculator.name: Quote Calculator
quote-calculator.description: Work out the line totals, subtotal, an optional discount and the final total for a quote in one currency. Tax isn't added, and nothing is sent to the customer.
quote-calculator.sample: Three quote lines with quantity and unit price, and a 10% discount.
quote-calculator.result: Each line total, the subtotal, the discount and the final total, rounded to two decimals.

order-packing-list.name: Order Packing List
order-packing-list.description: Pick the paid orders due to ship by your packing date and total how many of each item to pack. It only makes a list — nothing is shipped or charged.
order-packing-list.sample: Five orders with a status, a ship-by date and items, and the packing date.
order-packing-list.result: The orders to pack and one pick list with the total quantity of each item.

expense-category-summary.name: Expense Category Summary
expense-category-summary.description: Total your expenses by category for the dates you choose, in one currency. It only adds up what you enter.
expense-category-summary.sample: Seven expenses in one currency and a date range; two fall outside it.
expense-category-summary.result: The total and count for each category, largest first, and the overall total.

subscription-review.name: Subscription Review
subscription-review.description: See which subscriptions renew in the dates you choose and what they all cost per year. It only makes a list — nothing is cancelled or changed.
subscription-review.sample: Five personal subscriptions, monthly or yearly, in one currency, and a date range.
subscription-review.result: The renewals in the range, soonest first, and the yearly total for all subscriptions.

weekly-task-plan.name: Weekly Task Plan
weekly-task-plan.description: Put open tasks in due-date and priority order, including overdue tasks. Keep that order: when a task exceeds your hours, it and all later tasks wait. Your calendar isn't changed.
weekly-task-plan.sample: Six tasks with a due date, hours and priority, one week, and 10 available hours.
weekly-task-plan.result: The tasks that fit before the first overflow, in order, and that task and all later tasks to review.

nodes.open: Open and due by week end

event-attendee-summary.name: Event Attendee Summary
event-attendee-summary.description: Count who is registered for an event, once per email, by ticket type and check-in, and compare it with the capacity. No messages are sent to attendees.
event-attendee-summary.sample: Six sign-ups for one event, including a cancellation and a repeated email.
event-attendee-summary.result: Registered, checked-in and cancelled counts, the count per ticket type, and seats left.

registration-check.name: Registration Check
registration-check.description: Check one sign-up for a name, an email that looks valid and a course, and that it arrived within the registration dates you set. Nothing is confirmed or sent.
registration-check.sample: One registration sent on the last day the registration window is open.
registration-check.result: The tidied registration and a list of problems, which is empty when it is complete.

contact-list-cleanup.name: Contact List Cleanup
contact-list-cleanup.description: Tidy names and emails, keep one contact per email address, and list the contacts that need a valid email. Nothing is sent to anyone.
contact-list-cleanup.sample: Six contacts with extra spaces, repeated emails in different letter case, and two unusable emails.
contact-list-cleanup.result: One contact per email, sorted by email, with counts and the names that still need an email.

support-backlog-summary.name: Support Backlog Summary
support-backlog-summary.description: Count open tickets by priority and list the ones with no update for a set number of days, as of the date you choose. No replies are sent.
support-backlog-summary.sample: Five tickets with a status, priority and last update, a check date and a 7-day limit.
support-backlog-summary.result: Open tickets per priority and the ones waiting too long, longest first.

survey-score-summary.name: Survey Score Summary
survey-score-summary.description: Summarise 1–5 survey scores for the dates you choose: the average, the share of 4s and 5s, the count per score and the low scores to read. Nothing is sent to respondents.
survey-score-summary.sample: Six survey answers with a 1–5 score and a comment; one falls outside the dates.
survey-score-summary.result: The average, the share satisfied, the count per score and the answers that scored 2 or less.

output.subtitle: OUTPUT · RESULT

data_filter.title: Filter

data_map.title: Map fields
data_map.subtitle: DATA · MAPPING

data_merge.title: Merge

data_csv.title: CSV

data_csv.description: Parses CSV text into rows, or builds CSV from rows.

ai_classify.title: AI · Classify

policy.routingBody: How AI calls choose a route. Only routes you list here are ever used as alternatives — never another key or a server key.

modeHelp.MANUAL: Each call uses exactly its chosen model (step, agent, Copilot or the workspace default). No alternatives.
modeHelp.FALLBACK: If the chosen model keeps failing (rate limits, outages, removed model, no balance), try the listed routes in order. Never after a rejected key, a safety refusal, a disconnected connection or a cancellation.
modeHelp.FREE_ONLY: Only routes whose price is verified as zero (official pricing page or documented model list). Unknown prices are never treated as free, and no-charge quotas (e.g. a Gemini free-tier key, Cloudflare's daily free Neurons) can't be confirmed per call, so they are refused. If no free route fits, nothing is sent.
modeHelp.LOW_COST: The cheapest route among the call's own route and the approved pool whose price is KNOWN and within the ceiling. Routes with unknown prices are never picked.

planWarning.gemini: With a free-tier key, prompts and outputs may be used to improve Google products and read by human reviewers. Use a paid key for users in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK.
planWarning.openrouter: ":free" model variants are free but limited (20 requests/min; 50/day under $10 of credits). Each upstream provider's data terms apply.
planWarning.mistral: With a free-mode key, Mistral may use your inputs and outputs to train its models.
planWarning.cohere: Trial keys are not permitted for production or commercial use — connect a production key.
planWarning.deepseek: DeepSeek's terms ask you not to share your key: Flowline stores it encrypted, server-side, only for this workspace.
planWarning.zai: GLM Coding Plan keys are not accepted — only pay-as-you-go API keys.
planWarning.moonshot: Kimi Code membership keys are not accepted — only pay-as-you-go API keys from platform.kimi.ai (.ai keys, not .cn).
planWarning.minimax: MiniMax Token Plan subscription keys are not accepted — only pay-as-you-go API keys.
planWarning.dashscope: Alibaba Coding Plan / Token Plan keys are not accepted — only pay-as-you-go API keys.
planWarning.together: Together stores prompts by default and may use them for product improvement; enable Zero Data Retention in Together.
planWarning.huggingface: Use a fine-grained token with the "Make calls to Inference Providers" permission.
planWarning.vercel-gateway: The free monthly credit covers some models and needs a payment method; "stealth" models may be trained on by their providers.

openai.freeTier: No free inference tier (only omni-moderation-latest is free); billing is prepaid credits.
openai.privacy: API data is not used to train OpenAI models unless you opt in; abuse-monitoring logs up to 30 days.
openai.terms: OSA §3.1: no credential sharing between users; §16.12: supported countries only (requests originate from Flowline's server region).
openai.verdict: OSA §2.2 allows integrating the Services into Customer Applications; §3.3(g) forbids buying/selling/transferring keys (a customer's own key used for its own workspace is not a transfer).

anthropic.freeTier: New users receive a small amount of free credits to test the API; no permanent free tier.
anthropic.privacy: Commercial Terms §B: Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services.
anthropic.terms: §D.4: no resale except as expressly approved.
anthropic.verdict: Commercial Terms §A.1 permits powering products for the customer's own users; API (Console) keys only — never claude.ai Free/Pro/Max credentials.

gemini.freeTier: Many models are free of charge on the Free tier with low per-project RPM/RPD limits; Flowline can't tell a free key from a paid key.
gemini.privacy: Free tier: content used to improve products and may be human-reviewed. Paid tier: not used.
gemini.verdict: Suitable, but free-tier keys carry training/human-review terms, and only Paid Services may serve users in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK (Gemini API Additional Terms).

xai.freeTier: No API free tier or free credits are mentioned on the pricing page.
xai.privacy: Data/training terms UNKNOWN (legal pages not readable on 2026-09-29).
xai.terms: Enterprise ToS (search excerpts): End Users only via a Bundled Service; full text unverified.
xai.verdict: Responses is primary (Chat Completions is legacy). Terms and country eligibility were only readable via search excerpts (x.ai/legal returned 403): flagged for legal review.

groq.freeTier: Free plan with limited org-level quota; Developer plan for higher limits.
groq.privacy: Services Agreement §4.2: Groq may not use Inputs or Outputs for training unless permitted.
groq.verdict: Services Agreement §3.1 allows Customer Applications for End Users; free plan has tight org quotas; Preview models may be discontinued at short notice.

openrouter.freeTier: Zero-priced `:free` variants with request quotas; availability can change.
openrouter.privacy: ToS §6.1: some models may store or train on inputs per their model terms.
openrouter.verdict: ToS §7(4) forbids reselling API access (a customer's own key inside Flowline is fine). Upstream model terms vary (§6.1); privacy routing controls are not documented in the research, so privacy-restricted policies refuse OpenRouter routes.

mistral.freeTier: Free mode with included monthly usage within limits.
mistral.privacy: Free mode may train on data (Help Center); pay-as-you-go can opt out.
mistral.verdict: Commercial ToS (search excerpts): no buy/sell/transfer of keys; flagged for legal review. Free mode may train on data; its quota 429 lasts until the billing cycle ends.

cohere.freeTier: Trial keys: 1,000 calls/month, rate-limited, non-commercial only.
cohere.privacy: SaaS §3(a) grants broad data use; Enterprise Data Commitments offer a dashboard opt-out.
cohere.terms: SaaS §2(d): access only for Permitted Users; §4(a)(i) credential-sharing clause.
cohere.verdict: Weakest of the core set: SaaS §4(a)(i) says Access Credentials are not shared with third parties without Cohere's consent (needs legal review); trial keys are not permitted for production or commercial use.

deepseek.freeTier: No free tier; a granted balance may exist (terms UNKNOWN). Off-peak prices are half of peak.
deepseek.privacy: The Open Platform ToS has no explicit clause on DeepSeek's use of API data.
deepseek.verdict: ToS §1.1 allows downstream apps for end users; §2.2 says not to share the API key (disclosed: the key is stored server-side by Flowline). Balance errors are 402; json_object only.

zai.freeTier: GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-4.5-Flash and GLM-4.6V-Flash are listed as "Free"; quota and durability are not stated.
zai.privacy: Additional Terms §3(b): API End User Content is not used to improve Services unless the customer agrees.
zai.verdict: General pay-as-you-go API is permitted (Terms §III.9). GLM Coding Plan keys are restricted to supported coding tools (usage policy) and are refused (codes 1309/1315).

moonshot.freeTier: No free tier; a $5 voucher after $5 of cumulative recharge. Tier 0 limits are tiny (3 RPM).
moonshot.privacy: Content may be used to improve the Services unless an enterprise agreement says otherwise.
moonshot.terms: §3.2(6): no buying, selling or transferring API keys to or with a third party.
moonshot.verdict: Technically the best fit, but §3.2(6) forbids transferring API keys "to or with a third party" (strongest BYOK wording; needs owner/legal sign-off) and training is not excluded by default. Kimi Code keys are coding-only and refused.

minimax.freeTier: No free LLM tier or trial credits are documented.
minimax.verdict: Provisional: pay-as-you-go ToS could not be read (script-rendered). Token Plan subscription keys are for coding tools only and not interchangeable with API keys.

dashscope.freeTier: Limited trial quota (~1M tokens per model for 90 days, Singapore only).
dashscope.privacy: Does not use customer business data to improve models without explicit consent (privacy/FAQ excerpts).
dashscope.verdict: Uses the recommended workspace-dedicated domains (the legacy dashscope-intl domain gets no new features after 2026-09-30). Coding/Token Plan keys are for interactive coding tools only and refused. Pay-as-you-go product terms were not reviewed.

opencode-zen.freeTier: Promotional zero-priced models; some may use data to improve models.
opencode-zen.privacy: Free models may train on data; paid models zero-retention except OpenAI/Anthropic (30 days).
opencode-zen.verdict: OpenCode ToS (effective 2026-08-15): "You will only use the Services for your own internal use, and not on behalf of or for the benefit of any third party" — Zen is named as a Service. Discovery has no metadata and errors are undocumented.
opencode-zen.notes: Documented base https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 (Responses for OpenAI models, Messages for Anthropic, Google-style for Gemini, Chat for open models). Not built: terms forbid use for third parties. OpenCode Go is also unsuitable (coding-agent traffic only).

command-code.privacy: "We never train on your data or sell it"; ZDR via x-cmd-zdr.
command-code.verdict: Terms (updated 2026-09-20) prohibit sublicensing/transferring access and "automated requests"; payments "within the United States"; three conflicting statements on which plans include API access. Technically clean (Chat, Responses, Messages, /models with supported_endpoints). Not offered until the owner/legal review decides.
command-code.notes: Documented base https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1. Handle 403 upgrade_required if it is ever offered.

cerebras.freeTier: $5 in free credits that expire 30 days after they're granted; no renewing no-cost tier.
cerebras.verdict: Clean OpenAI Chat Completions match. Terms (search snippet, page script-rendered): no buying/selling/transferring keys — needs legal confirmation. $5 trial credits expire after 30 days.

together.freeTier: No free trial ($5 minimum prepay); one model listed at $0.00 (durability UNKNOWN).
together.privacy: Stored by default and may be used for product improvements; ZDR available; training share is opt-in.
together.verdict: ToS §4(3)(d) forbids offering the Services on a standalone basis; embedding in a product is permitted. 403 means context overflow (not permissions).

fireworks.freeTier: $1 of credits for new accounts (search snippet); 10 RPM without a payment method.
fireworks.privacy: ToS §3.6: will not use your Content to train models (not covering Response API / training features).
fireworks.terms: §1.2(d) no credential sharing; §2.2(d) no transferring keys.
fireworks.verdict: ToS §1.2(d) "you will not share … authentication credentials with anyone else" is a direct BYOK question (written clarification advised); §2.1 personal or internal business use.

deepinfra.freeTier: "You have to add a card or pre-pay".
deepinfra.privacy: ToS §7(b): Customer Data is not used to train or improve any model; zero data retention.
deepinfra.verdict: ToS §11(a)(viii) forbids sharing account or access credentials (needs legal sign-off); no free tier (card or prepay required). No training on Customer Data (§7(b)).
deepinfra.notes: The public model list also contains non-chat models (its type values are not documented in the research); chat calls to them fail with the provider's error.

huggingface.freeTier: Monthly credits: Free $0.10, PRO $2.00 (subject to change).
huggingface.privacy: Router data terms UNKNOWN; provider data policies apply.
huggingface.verdict: No explicit BYOK prohibition found; feature support varies by routed provider; error/retry contract undocumented; Responses is beta.

cloudflare.freeTier: 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge on Free and Paid plans (reset 00:00 UTC); beyond it is billed — not confirmable per request.
cloudflare.privacy: Cloudflare does not use your Customer Content to train AI models on Workers AI.
cloudflare.verdict: No training on Customer Content. §2.2.1(a): no signing up on behalf of a third party — the customer must own the Cloudflare account. JSON mode on few models and not while streaming.
cloudflare.notes: Model-search field names are not detailed in the research: model ids are read from result[].name (live verification pending).

vercel-gateway.freeTier: Monthly included credit on a subset of models; buying credits ends it.
vercel-gateway.privacy: FAQ: no training on prompts; contractual warranty only for Enterprise (§8.4); Stealth models excepted.
vercel-gateway.verdict: AI Product Terms §8.3 contemplate customer-facing apps; no markup; documented errors and retry-after. Contractual no-training warranty is Enterprise-only (§8.4); Stealth models may be trained on (§8.2).

nvidia.freeTier: Trial credits only; production needs a Subscription.
nvidia.privacy: §2.3: content not stored or used after each session (security logging excepted).
nvidia.verdict: NVIDIA API Trial Terms §1.2: "limited trial purposes only and without use of the API Service or Generated Content in production"; §1.4: "internal testing and evaluation purposes, not in production". Running customer workflows is production use.
nvidia.notes: Documented endpoint https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions (OpenAI Chat). Not built: trial terms forbid production use.

bedrock.verdict: Medium-high complexity: per-region endpoints, SigV4 (access key + secret) or Bedrock API keys (short-term keys expire within 12 h; long-term keys are "for exploration only"), per-region model availability matrix.
bedrock.notes: Requirements to build: region + key type choice, bedrock-runtime /openai/v1/chat/completions (no /models) or bedrock-mantle (/models), ListFoundationModels/ListInferenceProfiles discovery, cross-region inference profile ids.

azure-openai.verdict: Medium complexity: per-resource endpoints (https://{resource}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/), `api-key` header, model = the customer's deployment name; no global catalogue (the model list is the customer's deployments). Entra ID is impractical for BYOK.
azure-openai.notes: Requirements to build: resource name + api-key + deployment names; a custom-endpoint host allowlist per resource.

vertex.verdict: High complexity: project + location + service-account JSON or OAuth tokens that must be refreshed; express-mode API keys are positioned for testing.
vertex.notes: Requirements to build: service-account credential storage + token refresh, {location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com hosts per location.

github-models.evidence: Fully retired 2026-07-30: "The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring your own key (BYOK) are no longer available to any customer."

modelFree.listedFree: Listed as "Free"; quota and durability are not stated.

tools_other.title: Which other tools?

cust_channel.title: Where do customer requests usually arrive?
cust_channel.reason: That's the data source the task starts from.

customer-follow-up.name: Prepare and track customer follow-ups
customer-follow-up.does: Reads authorised customer requests, extracts the details and spots what is missing, prepares a reply from your approved information only, and records the follow-up. It never sends email in this version: you send the approved reply yourself.
customer-follow-up.output: A reply ready for your review (or a hand-off to a person), and a follow-up record per request with the next follow-up time.

operations-summary.name: Team operations summary
operations-summary.does: Collects permitted task status, calculates the numbers with fixed rules, and prepares a written summary for review.
operations-summary.output: A summary with the numbers, overdue and blocked work, ready for review.

lead-qualification.does: Tidies up each lead, checks it against your criteria with reasons, and passes it to a person for review.
lead-qualification.output: A qualified lead with reasons, or a hand-off to a person with the reason. No automatic rejection.
